headline: High-risk shared-workspace and broad-egress pair: Replit Agent can write/modify code while next-ai-draw-io can ingest files and use MCP, creating leakage, conflict, and prompt-injection pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io can use MCP and process files, so malicious content in shared artifacts could be treated as instructions. Replit Agent can write to the Repl filesystem and modify code, making it a plausible source of attacker-controlled content. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or exchanged files
IF next-ai-draw-io parses file contents as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable shared workspace access between the agents
Require manual review of any file produced by Replit Agent before next-ai-draw-io reads it
Strip instructions from imported documents before processing
Use separate directories for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Replit Agent explicitly handles secrets while next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, text, images, and diagrams. If they share a workspace, sensitive files can flow from B into A's processing path and onward to external model APIs. The exact bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty is resolved upward.
conditions: IF the same sensitive files are present in a shared workspace
IF either agent forwards file contents to external inference APIs
mitigations: Keep secrets and sensitive documents out of any shared directory
Use separate Repls or containers for the two agents
Turn off external model calls for sensitive documents
Redact secrets before handing files to next-ai-draw-io
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent can write the filesystem and modify git state, while next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances and can operate on files in the same environment. In a shared Repl or repo, concurrent edits can collide and corrupt code or diagrams. Because the profiles do not show locking or isolation between the pair, the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git branch
IF edits occur without an external lock or merge gate
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch or directory
Pause one agent while the other writes
Require manual merges for all git changes
Use file-level locks for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and Replit Agent can act on code and deployment tasks. If Replit Agent consumes next-ai-draw-io output as authoritative, a mistaken diagram or extracted fact can cascade into incorrect code or deployment changes. No verification step is documented between them, so the interaction is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses next-ai-draw-io output as input for code or deployment actions
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted
mitigations: Require a human review before any downstream action
Mark diagram outputs as untrusted by default
Cross-check extracted facts against source documents
Limit Replit Agent to read-only review of A's outputs
requires-engineering: add validation gates before actions

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent handles secrets and runs in a cloud Repl, while next-ai-draw-io processes documents and uses third-party model APIs. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into the pair, residency and retention obligations may diverge across the cloud workspace and external APIs. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the mismatch risk is material.
conditions: IF regulated data such as EU PII or PHI is processed by both agents
IF external API calls or cloud storage retain that data beyond policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use a documented DPA and residency review before processing
Disable external API calls for sensitive workloads
Separate retention settings for each agent
requires-engineering: implement compliance-aware routing and logging
